General.Description:
In 1923, the research vessel Stormcrow set out from Tromsø with twelve scientists and a bold mandate: to chart the unmapped interior of the Svalbard archipelago. Six months later, the Stormcrow was found drifting without crew, log, or cargo. No bodies were ever recovered. The expedition was declared lost, the files sealed, and the story quietly buried.

A century later, glaciologist Dr. Maren Solvay discovers a watertight cylinder embedded in a retreating glacier containing the private journals of the Stormcrow's lead scientist. What she reads sends her and historian James Kwon on a race against time — and against a powerful Norwegian energy consortium — to reach a location described in the final entries before the thawing ice erases it forever.

The Forgotten Expedition weaves together two timelines — 1923 and the present — with equal skill and equal tension. Co-authors Holden and Park bring complementary expertise: Holden's background in polar science grounds the historical chapters in visceral authenticity, while Park's gift for contemporary thriller plotting drives the modern narrative at relentless pace.

What happened on Svalbard in the winter of 1923? The answer is stranger — and more consequential — than either Solvay or Kwon could have imagined.

A luminous, gripping adventure story of the highest order.
